title: Single Inheritance
summary: Explore Single Inheritance in Java: one child extending one direct superclass, linear dispatch, predictable initialization, and real-world system designs.
learningObjectives: Define Single Inheritance and recognize its 1-to-1 parent-child structure
Understand why Java enforces single inheritance for class hierarchies
Trace linear method dispatch from subclass to superclass
Model real-world systems cleanly using single inheritance relationships
Analyze memory allocation and object creation under single inheritance
expectedOutcomes: Ability to explain the benefits of Single Inheritance in technical interviews
Confidence to design clean 1-to-1 superclass-subclass relationships in Java applications

activities.title: The Single Branch Analogy
activities.content:
Imagine a straight tree branch growing from a single trunk:

```text
Tree Trunk
    ↓
Single Branch
```

There is no confusion about where the branch gets its water or nutrients—it comes directly and solely from that one trunk! If you trace the branch back, there is only one clear, unambiguous path.

In Java, **Single Inheritance** means a subclass has **one direct superclass**. When the child needs a method or field, it looks at itself first, and if not found, looks directly at its one parent. There is never any confusion, conflicting instruction, or ambiguity!

activities.title: Single Inheritance: Architecture, Mechanics, and Advantages
Single Inheritance in Action: BankAccount and SavingsAccount
activities.description: Walk through a practical single inheritance implementation modeling banking accounts.

steps.description: BankAccount is the single superclass defining core account fields (accountNumber, balance) and deposit().
SavingsAccount extends BankAccount. It has one direct superclass, representing clean Single Inheritance.
SavingsAccount adds 'interestRate' and 'applyInterest()' without duplicating deposit() or balance.
In main(), savings can call both inherited methods (deposit, displayBalance) and its own method (applyInterest).

activities.title: Single Inheritance: Vehicle and ElectricCar
activities.description: Observe how an ElectricCar specializes a Vehicle through single inheritance.

steps.description: Vehicle acts as the single direct superclass with make, model, speed, accelerate(), and brake().
ElectricCar extends Vehicle, adding batteryPercentage and chargeBattery().
Single inheritance provides ElectricCar with full vehicle functionality while keeping electric logic separated.

questions.question: What defines Single Inheritance in Java?
options: A subclass can have only one field
A subclass has exactly one direct superclass
A program can only contain one class
A class can only be instantiated once
questions.explanation: Single Inheritance means a class extends exactly one direct parent class.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding Single Inheritance in Java?
options: A class can extend two classes if they are in the same package
A class can extend only one direct superclass
Java does not support single inheritance
Single inheritance requires the 'single' keyword
questions.explanation: Java strictly enforces that every class has at most one direct superclass.

questions.question: What happens when a method is called on an instance of a subclass?
options: Java searches the parent class first, then the child class
Java searches the subclass first; if not found, it checks its direct superclass
Java executes all methods with that name in all classes simultaneously
Java throws an exception if the method is in the parent
questions.explanation: Linear dispatch starts at the subclass level and moves upward to the direct superclass if not found.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of single inheritance over multiple inheritance?
options: Programs compile without needing Java installed
Predictability and elimination of method resolution ambiguity
Variables can hold any type without casting
Garbage collection is disabled
questions.explanation: Single inheritance eliminates ambiguity, making dispatch order deterministic and predictable.

questions.question: In the hierarchy 'Class B extends Class A', what is Class A called?
options: Subclass
Direct superclass
Sibling class
Interface
questions.explanation: Class A is the direct superclass (parent) of Class B.

questions.question: Can multiple different subclasses extend the same single superclass?
options: No, only one child class can ever extend a parent
Yes, multiple classes can each have the same class as their single direct superclass
Only if the classes are static
Only if the parent is an interface
questions.explanation: Yes! For example, Dog extends Animal and Cat extends Animal. Each child has one direct superclass (Animal).

questions.question: Does single inheritance prevent code from growing too complex?
options: Yes, by maintaining a simple, linear hierarchy without conflicting inheritance branches
No, single inheritance is completely unmaintainable
It forces all code into a single file
It makes programs run slower
questions.explanation: Single inheritance prevents the tangled dependencies common in multiple inheritance languages.

questions.question: If Class Dog extends Animal, does Dog also inherit from java.lang.Object?
options: No, Dog only inherits from Animal
Yes, because Animal extends Object, making Object the indirect superclass of Dog
Only if Dog implements Object
Only if Object is explicitly imported
questions.explanation: Animal extends Object, so Dog transitively inherits from Object through Animal.

questions.question: What keyword connects a subclass to its single direct superclass in Java?
options: super
extends
inherits
with
questions.explanation: The 'extends' keyword specifies the single direct superclass.

questions.question: Can a subclass in a single inheritance relationship override a superclass method?
options: No, overriding requires multiple inheritance
Yes, a subclass can provide its own specialized implementation of any accessible non-final parent method
Only if the method has no parameters
Only if the method is private
questions.explanation: A subclass can override any accessible non-final method inherited from its single direct superclass.

interviewQA.question: What is Single Inheritance in Java and what makes it advantageous?
interviewQA.answer: Single inheritance is an object-oriented pattern where a class is derived from exactly one direct superclass. Its main advantages are simplicity, clear linear method dispatch, clean memory organization, and complete elimination of diamond inheritance ambiguity.

interviewQA.question: How does method resolution work in single inheritance?
interviewQA.answer: When a method is called on an object reference, the JVM starts searching for the method body in the object's actual runtime class. If not found, it traverses directly up to its single direct superclass, continuing up the chain until it reaches java.lang.Object or reports a compile-time error.

interviewQA.question: Can a class have multiple subclasses while still adhering to single inheritance?
interviewQA.answer: Yes. Single inheritance dictates that each class can have at most one direct superclass. However, a single superclass can have arbitrarily many direct subclasses (e.g., Dog, Cat, and Bird all extend Animal).

interviewQA.question: Is single inheritance in Java limited strictly to two levels?
interviewQA.answer: No. While each class has only one direct superclass, inheritance can form multi-tier chains (e.g., A -> B -> C), known as Multilevel Inheritance, where every step remains a single inheritance relationship.

interviewQA.question: How do constructors behave in single inheritance?
interviewQA.answer: Constructors are executed sequentially from the top of the hierarchy down to the target subclass. Before executing the subclass constructor body, the superclass constructor must run, invoked either explicitly via super() or implicitly by the compiler inserting super().

interviewQA.question: What design problems occur when developers abuse single inheritance?
interviewQA.answer: Overusing single inheritance for code reuse rather than genuine taxonomic IS-A relationships leads to fragile base classes, tight architectural coupling, and bloated superclasses. When code reuse without genuine subtyping is needed, composition is preferred.

activities.title: 10-Point Mastery Checklist: Single Inheritance
checklist: I can define Single Inheritance clearly
I know that each Java class has at most one direct superclass
I understand why Java chose single inheritance over multiple class inheritance
I can trace linear method dispatch from subclass to superclass
I can build a working single inheritance hierarchy in Java
I know that one superclass can have multiple direct child classes
I understand how fields and methods are shared in a 1-to-1 relationship
I know how constructor calls chain up to the single direct parent
I can differentiate appropriate IS-A single inheritance from composition
I understand the memory layout of a subclass instance under single inheritance

practiceProblems.title: Single Inheritance: Computer and Desktop
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Create a parent class `Computer` with field `String processor` and method `void boot()` that prints `"Computer booting with " + processor`.
Create a child class `Desktop` extending `Computer` with field `int monitorCount` and method `void showMonitors()` that prints `"Desktop connected to " + monitorCount + " monitor(s)"`.
In `Main.main()`, instantiate `Desktop`, assign `processor = "Intel Core i7"` and `monitorCount = 2`, then invoke `boot()` followed by `showMonitors()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Computer booting with Intel Core i7
Desktop connected to 2 monitor(s)
hints: dt.processor is inherited directly from Computer.

practiceProblems.title: Single Inheritance: Printer and LaserPrinter
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Write a complete program from scratch:
1. Create a superclass `Printer` with field `String model` and method `void printDocument(String doc)` printing `model + " printing: " + doc`.
2. Create a subclass `LaserPrinter` extending `Printer` with field `int tonerLevel` and method `void printTonerStatus()` printing `"Toner level at: " + tonerLevel + "%"`.
3. In `Main.main()`, create a `LaserPrinter`, set `model = "HP LaserJet 400"` and `tonerLevel = 85`, call `printDocument("Quarterly_Report.pdf")`, and call `printTonerStatus()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
HP LaserJet 400 printing: Quarterly_Report.pdf
Toner level at: 85%
hints: LaserPrinter inherits model and printDocument() from Printer.

practiceProblems.title: Specialized Book and EBook Modeling
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Create a parent class `Book` with fields `String title`, `String author`, and a method `void showOverview()` printing `"'" + title + "' by " + author`.
Create a child class `EBook` extending `Book` with field `double fileSizeMB` and method `void download()` printing `"Downloading " + title + " (" + fileSizeMB + " MB)..."`.
In `Main.main()`, instantiate an `EBook`, set `title = "Effective Java"`, `author = "Joshua Bloch"`, `fileSizeMB = 4.2`, and call `showOverview()` followed by `download()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
'Effective Java' by Joshua Bloch
Downloading Effective Java (4.2 MB)...
hints: EBook inherits title and author from Book.

practiceProblems.title: Bug Hunt: Linear Dispatch Confusion
practiceProblems.problemStatement: The following program attempts to model a `Vehicle` and `Bicycle` relationship under single inheritance, but contains errors preventing proper compilation and output. Fix the class declaration and variable access so it runs and produces the expected output.
hints: Replace 'implement' with 'extends' in the Bicycle class declaration.
Since speed is protected in Vehicle, Bicycle can access it directly.

practiceProblems.title: Architecting an Order and ExpressOrder Pipeline
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Implement an order pipeline using single inheritance:
1. Parent class `Order`:
   - `protected String orderId`
   - `protected double amount`
   - Constructor `public Order(String orderId, double amount)`
   - Method `public double calculateTotal()` returning `amount`
   - Method `public void printReceipt()` printing `"Order: " + orderId + ", Total: $" + calculateTotal()`
2. Child class `ExpressOrder` extending `Order`:
   - `private double expressFee`
   - Constructor `public ExpressOrder(String orderId, double amount, double expressFee)` calling `super(orderId, amount)`
   - Override `calculateTotal()` to return `amount + expressFee`
   - Method `public void trackDelivery()` printing `"Tracking express order " + orderId + " with expedited courier."`
3. In `Main.main()`, instantiate `ExpressOrder("EXP-9001", 120.0, 15.0)`, call `printReceipt()`, and call `trackDelivery()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Order: EXP-9001, Total: $135.0
Tracking express order EXP-9001 with expedited courier.
hints: ExpressOrder overrides calculateTotal() to include expressFee.
printReceipt() in Order calls calculateTotal(), which dynamically executes ExpressOrder's overridden method!
